pattern.short_summary: A goal supplied at runtime is broken into smaller sub-parts, and the parts are produced or handled serially rather than in one shot.
pattern.definition: A goal supplied at runtime is broken into smaller sub-parts, and the parts are produced or handled serially rather than in one shot. The decomposition is derived from the particular goal, so its shape varies with the input. Each part surfaces as its own step that can be inspected or edited before the next is taken.
pattern.structural_signature: An input goal is transformed into an ordered list of sub-parts whose length and identity are computed per input (by the system, the user, or both). Each sub-part is executed or generated separately, in sequence, and appears as a discrete step in the interface; the final artifact is assembled from the parts. The sequence exists only for this goal — a different goal yields a different sequence.

dimension.category_description: How visible stages, dialogue states, histories, task decompositions, and session boundaries organize progress over time.
dimension.classification_boundary: The process structure must be exposed to users; hidden chains of model calls are excluded.
